newsitem.title: USA: US rail intermodal freight up - AAR.
newsitem.headline: US rail intermodal freight up - AAR.

text.p: U.S. and Canadian freight rail traffic are moving at record levels at the mid-year mark compared to previous years, the Association of American Railroads said Thursday.

AAR said U.S. carloads rose 2.6 percent in the week to 347,898 from 339,217 in the year-ago week, while ton-miles were up 3.5 percent to 26.5 in the week ended June 28 from 25.6 a year ago. The ton-mile, a measure of freight transportation, is one ton of freight hauled one mile.
The largest increases in carloadings reported by the AAR were 10.1 percent for crushed stone, sand and gravel, 9.1 percent for metals and products, and 8.2 percent for farm products excluding grain.
Carloads declined 12.2 percent for metallic ores, 6.8 percent for primary forest products, and 5.7 percent for food and kindred products.
U.S. intermodal traffice rose 7.0 percent to 175,796 in the week ended June 28 compared to 164,295 in the year ago week.

AAR reported that the two Canadian transcontinental railroads had 53,210 carloads in the June 28 week, up 6.8 percent from the year-ago week, and 24,361 trailers and containers, up 11.3 percent from last year.

Combined U.S. and Canada carloadings in the first 26 weeks of 1997 were 10.21 million, up 1.6 percent from the comparable period last year. Combined intermodal treaffic was up 7.3% to 4.87 trailers and containers.
